title: RelayShield Scam Checks Now Live in ChatGPT and Claude
excerpt: Free RelayShield plugins are now live for ChatGPT and Claude, plus v0.3.1 of the Chrome extension. Check links, wallets, and emails for scams without leaving your AI assistant.
html:
RelayShield Scam Checks Now Live in ChatGPT and Claude

Your AI assistant can now check whether that link, wallet, or email is a scam, without leaving the chat.

We have shipped free RelayShield plugins for both major AI assistants. ChatGPT users get "RelayShield Scam Checks." Claude users get relayshield-guard. Both are live today, both are free, and both are backed by the same threat intelligence corpus: 124 monitored Telegram marketplaces, 687K+ indicators, and 8.6M citations.

What is live

ChatGPT plugin: RelayShield Scam Checks (v1.0.0)

Install it from the ChatGPT plugin store and ask it to check anything suspicious: a URL from a DM, a crypto wallet address from an investment pitch, an email address from an unsolicited message, or whether an email appears in known breach data. The plugin calls RelayShield's free endpoints and reports back with a verdict. No signup, no API key for basic checks.

Claude plugin: relayshield-guard (v1.1.0)

This one works differently. Instead of waiting for you to ask, it screens before tool calls execute. When Claude is about to fetch a URL, run a command, or use a tool on your behalf, relayshield-guard checks the call first. It catches prompt injection attempts hidden in tool responses, malicious URLs in arguments, and wallet addresses tied to known scams. It is a strict superset of our earlier pre-bind screening plugin, adding Solana and BTC wallets, applicant emails, and a source marker so you can see what was checked.

MCP server in the official registry

For everyone else, the same checks are available as an MCP server: `io.github.nzdsf2-gif/relayshield-free-mcp` (v1.30.0) is published in the official MCP Registry. Any MCP-compatible client can connect and get free scam checks for links, wallets, emails, and breach exposure. No signup.

How it works

All three integrations call the same free RelayShield API endpoints. When you submit a URL, the service checks it against the threat intelligence corpus: is this domain associated with a known phishing kit, a scam marketplace listing, or a recent fraud campaign? Wallets get screened against addresses tied to scams and theft. Emails get checked for breach exposure and scam associations.

Every check returns one of three verdicts:

  • BLOCKED: Strong signal this is malicious. Do not proceed.
  • FLAGGED: Suspicious indicators found. Treat with caution and verify independently.
  • ALLOWED: No flags found in the corpus. This is not a guarantee, only that nothing matched.

We are deliberate about that last point. No check can prove something is legitimate, so we never say it is. ALLOWED means the corpus had nothing on it, nothing more.

Why this matters now

AI assistants are becoming the front door for how people research, shop, and transact online. That makes them a natural place to ask "is this a scam?" before clicking, sending, or buying. The alternative is copying a suspicious link into a separate tool, which most people will not do in the moment.

Putting the check inside the conversation removes that friction. You paste the link, you get a verdict, you decide. The 500-call-per-day partner tier keeps the free plugins fast for everyone.

Also in your browser

The same tri-state verdicts are now in the Chrome extension. Version 0.3.1, live in the Chrome Web Store, adds a first-run consent screen on top of the BLOCKED, FLAGGED, and ALLOWED verdicts that shipped in v0.3.0. Right-click any link, paste a wallet address, or screen a suspicious email, the same checks as the plugins and the free MCP server.

Try it

  • Chrome: install the RelayShield extension from the Chrome Web Store
  • ChatGPT: install "RelayShield Scam Checks" from the plugin store
  • Claude: install relayshield-guard (v1.1.0)
  • Any MCP client: connect to `io.github.nzdsf2-gif/relayshield-free-mcp` from the official registry
  • Developers: get an API key and full documentation at api.relayshield.net/developers

If you run a team or product that could use scam screening inside your own AI workflows, the same endpoints power our paid tiers with higher limits and the full 30-endpoint API. Start free, upgrade when the volume justifies it.
